content:
Requirement R13 (output): Communicate UAV Status. Fixed modalities: Screen and Audio-out. Intent: Convey the current status of a UAV to the pilot..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-13.1, F-13.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-13.<F>.1, Be-13.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-13.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Convey the current status of a UAV to the pilot (output only, via Screen + Audio-out).

Function candidates:

**F-13.1 — Maintain continuous UAV status awareness.**
Goal: keep the pilot passively informed of the UAV's live operating state (link, mode, health, position/attitude summary) so it is available at a glance whenever attention turns to it. Persistent, always-on presence.

**F-13.2 — Alert the pilot to UAV status changes/anomalies.**
Goal: actively draw the pilot's attention when the UAV state transitions or degrades (link loss, mode change, fault, low fuel). Event-driven, not continuous.

These are genuinely distinct: F-13.1 is about ambient availability of state; F-13.2 is about capturing attention on a discrete change. Note R12 (status panel visibility toggle) and R08 (notification stack) sit adjacent — F-13.1 supplies the *content* R12 shows/hides; F-13.2 is a status-specific consumer of the R08 alert pattern. Worth flagging both as sharing candidates.

I'd resist a third "query-on-demand" function — that's pull interaction (5.1/4.2 style) and would be an input-triggered Function, which conflicts with R13 being output-only.

Which Function do you want to close on?

Agreed — both survive as distinct Functions. They cover different pilot needs (ambient monitoring vs. attention capture) and neither collapses into the other.

**Closed:**
- **F-13.1 — Maintain continuous UAV status awareness** (persistent, ambient).
- **F-13.2 — Alert the pilot to UAV status changes/anomalies** (event-driven, attention-capturing).

Moving to Behaviour. I'll propose flows for each.

**For F-13.1 (continuous awareness):**

**Be-13.1.1 — Persistent multi-field status render.**
UAV status fields (link, mode, health, fuel, position/attitude summary) are continuously displayed on Screen in a fixed panel; values update in place as the aircraft feeds new data. No audio in steady state (would be nuisance if continuous). Measurable: refresh latency, field completeness, legibility.

**Be-13.1.2 — Persistent Screen + on-demand audio summary.**
Same persistent Screen render, but adds a spoken status summary triggered by pilot action. — *I'd reject this*: the trigger is input, which pulls it out of R13's output-only scope. Flag only, not a real candidate.

So F-13.1 effectively has one clean output-only flow: **Be-13.1.1**.

**For F-13.2 (change/anomaly alert):**

**Be-13.2.1 — Redundant alert on transition (audio tone + visual flag).**
On a status change/fault, fire a one-shot audio cue plus a visual highlight/flag on the status field that changed. Reuses R08 notification pattern. Modality-complete across Screen+Audio. Measurable: alert-to-onset latency, salience, dismissal behaviour.

**Be-13.2.2 — Severity-graded alert.**
Same as .1 but differentiates tone/visual treatment by severity (advisory vs. caution vs. warning) — e.g. link-loss = warning, mode change = advisory. Measurable: correct severity discrimination, false-alarm rate.

My recommendation: **Be-13.1.1** for F-13.1, and **Be-13.2.2** for F-13.2 (severity grading matters in a high-workload cockpit where not every status change deserves equal interruption).

Your call on the Behaviours.

Noted — F-13.1 closes on **Be-13.1.1**; F-13.2 keeps both **Be-13.2.1** and **Be-13.2.2** as parallel behaviours (flat alert vs. severity-graded). They can coexist: .2.2 is essentially .2.1 with a severity dimension layered on, so the structure will share components.

Moving to Structure.

**For Be-13.1.1 (persistent multi-field render):**

**S-13.1.1.1 — Extend the R12 UAV Detail/Status Panel.**
Reuse the existing UAV Status Panel (already the R12 show/hide target) as the canonical status surface. Populate it with the live field set (link, mode, health, fuel, position/attitude summary), updating in place. Screen only, WAD-resident. This is the natural home — R12 already governs its visibility, R13 supplies its content.

**S-13.1.1.2 — HUD status strip.**
A compact always-on status line on the HUD (link + mode + a health rollup), for head-up glance without diverting to WAD. Complements .1.1.1 rather than replacing it — reduced field set for HUD real estate.

Recommendation: **both** — S-13.1.1.1 as the full render on WAD (shared with R12), S-13.1.1.2 as the head-up abbreviated strip. Flag: the WAD panel is a shared structure with R12/R08.

**For Be-13.2.1 + Be-13.2.2 (alert on change, flat + graded):**

**S-13.2.x.1 — Reuse R08 notification stack, severity-parameterized.**
Audio: shared R08 tone channel, with distinct tones per severity tier (advisory/caution/warning) for .2.2; a single tone for .2.1. Visual: field-level highlight/flag on the S-13.1.1.1 panel (colour-coded by severity for .2.2) plus the reusable R08 pop-up/notification-marker for higher tiers. No new hardware.

**S-13.2.x.2 — HUD-escalated warning.**
For warning-tier events (e.g. link loss), push the flag to the HUD strip (S-13.1.1.2) so it's caught head-up, not just on WAD. Ties the alert into the head-up path.

Recommendation: **S-13.2.x.1** as the base (covers both .2.1 flat and .2.2 graded via parameterization), **S-13.2.x.2** as the escalation layer for top-severity events. All reused/shared with R08 and the R13 status panel — no new structure invented.

Your call on the Structures.

**R13 closed.**

**Functions**
- **F-13.1** — Maintain continuous UAV status awareness.
- **F-13.2** — Alert the pilot to UAV status changes/anomalies.

**Behaviours**
- **Be-13.1.1** — Persistent multi-field status render (Screen, no steady-state audio). → F-13.1
- **Be-13.2.1** — Redundant alert on transition (flat audio tone + visual flag). → F-13.2
- **Be-13.2.2** — Severity-graded alert (tone/visual differentiated by advisory/caution/warning). → F-13.2

**Structures**
- **S-13.1.1.1** — Extended R12 UAV Detail/Status Panel, live field set, WAD (shared with R12/R08).
- **S-13.1.1.2** — HUD abbreviated status strip (link/mode/health rollup), head-up complement.
- **S-13.2.x.1** — R08 notification stack, severity-parameterized: tone tiers + field-level colour-coded highlight/flag + pop-up/marker (covers both Be-13.2.1 and Be-13.2.2).
- **S-13.2.x.2** — HUD-escalated warning for top-severity events (reuses S-13.1.1.2 strip).

**Sharing flags:** WAD status panel shared with R12 (visibility) and R08 (notifications); audio/pop-up/marker components inherited from R08; HUD strip serves both continuous awareness (F-13.1) and alert escalation (F-13.2). No new hardware introduced.
